beats.prompt: Set the lever against the chimney sill
beats.result: The square of dry wood beneath the soot is a register cover. You get a knee under it before the weight shifts again.

beats.prompt: Separate the receipt from the later addition
beats.line: A patrol clerk counted a delivery. A different hand filled the empty margin.
beats.result: Vale will need both hands preserved on the copy.

choices.label: Copy the margin and receipt on separate leaves
Trace both hands together and mark the change of ink
choices.result: The join is visible and labelled.

evidence.title: The sanctuary receipt
evidence.text: The old hand acknowledges receipt. A later hand added an oral claim. Neither entry records a safe onward journey.

beats.prompt: Ask who added the words in the margin
beats.line: I saw the red cord. I knew Avel when he said it. I wrapped the crow again and promised I’d come behind them. I waited. Then I went looking. It matters which I did first.
beats.result: She names her own act. The search afterward cannot turn a promise into a return.
beats.speaker: Anwen

beats.prompt: Ask which words are hers to release
beats.line: I wrote that Harl held the gate. Close it, Kael. That’s the verb I mean. The letter in the other fold is a letter from my husband.
beats.result: The first paragraph is hers to give. She slips the other fold back inside her bodice.
beats.speaker: Elna

choices.label: Take only the paragraph she offers
choices.result: Elna marks the fair copy with her initials.

beats.prompt: Cover the household addresses before copying
beats.result: The figures and delivery dates remain legible.

beats.prompt: Compare the flour charge against the receipt
beats.result: One soldier bought his own bread. His purchase cannot stand for an entire levy.

evidence.title: A baker’s sale
evidence.text: The soldier paid for his own loaf. The bakery copy retains amounts and dates without household addresses.

beats.prompt: Take up the capstan slack
beats.result: The first lashing holds. The sill shifts under the second.

beats.prompt: Catch the slipping freight
beats.line: The sill is coming out. There is time to steady one load. The other will go into the water.

choices.label: Catch the medicine chest
choices.result: The jars stay dry. Tor must borrow tools for the repair.

choices.label: Catch the tool chest
choices.result: The planes and augers stay dry. Mira will stretch the clean stores.

beats.prompt: Strike the lost load from the receiving sheet
beats.result: There is a wet mark beside the short delivery. Nobody will set out looking for a chest that never came.

beats.prompt: Leave room at the end of the supper bench
beats.line: You can sit down even if your arm doesn’t need seeing to. You will have to cut the onions.
beats.result: There is work for two hands at supper.
beats.speaker: Mira

choices.label: Cut onions together
choices.result: She keeps the uneven slices for the bottom of the pot.

choices.label: Bring a covered bowl for later
choices.result: Mira can eat after the last call.

beats.prompt: Pass drinking water down the south-yard bench
beats.result: Six hands take the cup. A seventh is holding a strip of cloth against someone’s head.

beats.prompt: Check the workers against the wage marks
beats.result: Seven made it out. A wage mark is still owed to each of them.

evidence.title: Seven out of the gallery
evidence.text: The crew was counted in the yard after the escape. Seven workers reached clean air.

beats.prompt: Match the wage page to the mill measure
beats.result: The half-notch marks belong to the mill. The handwriting beside them is a clerk’s.

beats.prompt: Leave a checked copy with the wheelkeeper
beats.result: He can answer for the measures he used. He was never at the sanctuary.

evidence.title: The wheelkeeper’s copy
evidence.text: The wheelkeeper can attest the mill measures. His account does not reach the old gate.

beats.prompt: Hold the fallen sill off the wheelkeeper
beats.result: The wheelkeeper rolls clear. Tor lets go with his left hand and cannot close it again.

beats.prompt: Fit two cratewood splints around Tor’s left wrist
beats.result: “Straight enough,” Tor says, looking past his arm at the gallery. “Someone still has to cut that sill square.”

beats.prompt: Mark the sill to Tor’s right-hand measurement
beats.result: Another pair of hands does the cutting. His mark still governs the fit.

beats.prompt: Return the bell by its worn leather handle
beats.line: You could have asked for another day. I’m glad you didn’t.
beats.result: Elna puts the real bell back on its nail. You retain the rubbing from the cemetery.
beats.speaker: Elna

beats.prompt: Scrape the worst of the crust over the bucket
beats.result: The inside is still soft. The heel will make a reasonable doorstop.

beats.prompt: Turn the grain proclamation over
beats.line: Grain on the front. A place for assent on the back. The store count is real. So is the condition.
beats.result: Nera’s margin reads: passage first. Nobody’s meal signs for them.

choices.label: Mark the condition for the crew
choices.result: The people who haul this grain will know the price.

choices.label: Post a clean copy beside the portions
choices.result: The figures and condition can be read together.

beats.prompt: Open the smoky end of the cooking shelter
beats.result: The smoke lifts above the bench. A tired cook can breathe there.

beats.prompt: Set a relief turn at the serving table
beats.line: Nessa has worked the first pot. Someone has to mind the second.

choices.label: Take the next service yourself
choices.result: Nessa turns the ladle loose and goes outside with her own bowl.

choices.label: Divide the shift at the second pot
choices.result: The first cook gets a seat before the next pot boils.

beats.prompt: Let the waiting worker measure the portions
beats.result: The worker levels the ladle. A fair portion leaves the pot sooner than an argument does.

beats.prompt: Ask why he needs the crew together
beats.line: I took the houses off it. The names too. Merrow wanted a time and a place, and I wanted bread. I sent the times. I did that before asking.
beats.result: He pays for grain with his own silver. It still was not his schedule to trade.
beats.speaker: Rook

beats.prompt: Lay the exposed schedule in front of the crew
beats.line: Only the crew needs the times. They need them before they choose a road.

choices.label: Tell them where the copy went, keeping the names private
choices.result: Nera carries the route book herself.

choices.label: Have Rook read his alteration aloud beside the route book
choices.result: The people who carry the grain hear exactly what he sold.

beats.prompt: Check the bank around the living willow
beats.result: The trunk holds. It is the earth around the roots that must be checked after rain.

beats.prompt: Lay the hauling line clear of the guide
beats.result: One line guides the hull. The other moves it. Neither does the other’s work.

beats.prompt: Mark the landing for freight and passengers
beats.result: Four aboard with freight. Six adults travelling light, crew included. The receiving cart waits beyond the soft hollow.
